column2: A man who thus bows to the twelve Adityas, and constantly hears and recites this, is honoured in the Sun's world.
If this Sun is the primal, eternal god, then why did he practise austerity, desiring a boon, like an ordinary being?
I shall tell you this supreme secret of Vibhavasu, which Mitra formerly told when asked by the great-souled Narada.
The twelve forms of the Sun were told to you earlier by me; Mitra and Varuna, both of them, were established in austerity.
Varuna, living on water, stayed in the western ocean; Mitra, living on wind, stayed in this Mitra forest.
Then Narada, the great yogi, self-controlled, roaming all worlds, having descended from the peak of Mount Meru, Gandhamadana,
came to that very place where Mitra was practising austerity. Seeing him performing austerity, curiosity arose in him:

He who is imperishable and immutable, manifest and unmanifest, eternal, by whom the three worlds are held as one self, the great-souled —
brahmapuran:30:52	he who is father of all gods, supreme even among the supreme: whom does he worship, or which ancestors? Thinking thus in his mind, Narada said to that god:

In the Vedas with Puranas, with their limbs and subsidiary limbs, you are sung as unborn, eternal, the Creator, the unsurpassed treasure.
brahmapuran:30:54	Past, future and present — all is established in you. The four ashramas, god, beginning with the householder,
brahmapuran:30:55	worship you day by day; you have taken up a bodily form. You are father and mother of all, the eternal deity.
brahmapuran:30:56	Whom do you worship as father, or what god? We do not know.

This is not to be spoken, yet it must be told, the supreme secret, eternal; to you who have devotion, Brahmin, I shall tell it as it is.
brahmapuran:30:58	That which is subtle, unknowable, unmanifest, immovable, firm, devoid of the senses, sense-objects and all beings —
brahmapuran:30:59	he is the inner self of beings and is called the knower of the field; distinct from the three qualities, he is conceived as the Purusha.
brahmapuran:30:60	The lord Hiranyagarbha is that very Buddhi, it is remembered; in yoga he is called Mahat, and is called Pradhana.
brahmapuran:30:61	In Sankhya and in Yoga he is spoken of by many names, many-natured; he is threefold, the Self of the universe, remembered as Sharva and the imperishable.
brahmapuran:30:62	By him as one self these three worlds are held. Bodiless, he dwells in all bodies.
brahmapuran:30:63	Though dwelling in bodies, he is not smeared by actions. The inner self of me, of you, and of others abiding in bodies —
brahmapuran:30:64	he is the witness of all, not to be grasped by anyone anywhere; with qualities and without, the universal, he is remembered as attainable by knowledge.
brahmapuran:30:65	With hands and feet on every side, with eyes, heads and faces on every side, with ears on every side in the world, he abides enveloping all.
brahmapuran:30:66	With universal head, universal arms, universal feet, eyes and nose, he moves alone in the field, a free wanderer, at will.
brahmapuran:30:67	Bodies here are fields; he, the yogic Self, knows them at will, therefore he is called the Knower of the Field.
brahmapuran:30:68	He lies in the unmanifest city, and so is called Purusha. The universe is manifold, to be known, and he is said to be everywhere.
brahmapuran:30:69	Therefore, because of many forms, he is remembered as Vishvarupa (of universal form). This one's greatness is such that he alone is remembered as the Purusha.
brahmapuran:30:70	The one eternal bears the name Great Purusha. He, depending on ordinance and action, creates himself by himself.
brahmapuran:30:71	A hundredfold, a thousandfold, and a hundred-thousandfold, even by crores, he makes himself, the inner Self, by himself.
brahmapuran:30:72	As water falling from the sky takes on a different taste in different earth by special flavour, so he does by the flavour of the qualities.
brahmapuran:30:73	As the one wind becomes fivefold in bodies, so oneness and difference are his; no doubt.
brahmapuran:30:74	As fire gets a distinct name from the difference of place, so, sage, this one obtains (names) as Brahma and others.
brahmapuran:30:75	As from one lamp thousands of lamps are kindled, so this one gives birth to thousands of forms.
brahmapuran:30:76	When he awakens to himself, then he becomes the Solitary; at the dissolution of oneness, multiplicity arises for him.
brahmapuran:30:77	In the world nothing, moving or unmoving, is eternal; he alone is called imperishable, immeasurable and all-pervading.
brahmapuran:30:78	Therefore the Unmanifest, three-gunaed, arose, best of Brahmins; the state of the manifest and unmanifest is called Prakriti.
brahmapuran:30:79	Know that as the womb of Brahma, who is of the nature of being and non-being, who is worshipped in the world, in rites for gods and ancestors.
brahmapuran:30:80	There is no other father or god higher than him, Brahmins; he is to be known by the Self, and therefore I worship him.
brahmapuran:30:81	Even in the heavens, any embodied beings who bow to him go by that, sage of the gods, to the goal with the fruit they intended.
brahmapuran:30:82	Gods, staying in their own abodes, resorting to many forms, worship that Primal One with devotion, and he grants them their goal.
brahmapuran:30:83	For he is said to be all-pervading and without qualities. Thinking thus, according to my knowledge, I worship the Day-maker.
brahmapuran:30:84	Those people who are absorbed in him and take refuge in the one truth — this too is more for them, that they enter the One.
brahmapuran:30:85	Thus this secret instruction has been told to you, Narada; and by our devotion, sage of the gods, it is held supreme by you also.
brahmapuran:30:86	By gods, by sages and in the Puranas it is remembered as boon-giving; all worship the Day-maker as the Supreme Self.
brahmapuran:30:87	This was thus told formerly by the Sun to Narada, and this story of the Sun has been told by me too, best of Brahmins.
brahmapuran:30:88	This account that I have told is to be told, best of Brahmins; it must never be given to one not devoted to the Sun.
brahmapuran:30:89	The man who constantly makes this heard, and he who hears it, enters the god of a thousand rays; there is no doubt.
brahmapuran:30:90	One distressed is freed, and likewise one sick, by hearing this story from the beginning; one eager to know gains knowledge and the desired goal.
brahmapuran:30:91	He who reads this, sage, gains the way in an instant; whoever desires any desire obtains it without doubt.
brahmapuran:30:92	Therefore the revered Sun should be constantly remembered by you; he is the Creator and the Disposer, the lord of the whole world.
brahmapuran:31:11	The sun does not burn from lack of rain, does not dry up from lack of rain, does not wear a halo from lack of rain; the Sun shines with water.
brahmapuran:31:12	In spring the Sun is tawny, in summer like gold, in the rains white in colour, in autumn the Sun is pale,
brahmapuran:31:13	in the cool season coppery, in winter red: thus the colours of the Sun that arise from the seasons are told.
brahmapuran:31:14	With the colours that belong to the seasons the Sun brings welfare and plentiful food. Now the general names of Aditya, best of Brahmins:
brahmapuran:31:15	I shall tell the twelve separately, entirely: Aditya, Savita, Surya, Mihira, Arka, Prabhakara,
brahmapuran:31:16	Martanda, Bhaskara, Bhanu, Chitrabhanu, Divakara, Ravi: the Sun is known by these twelve general names.
brahmapuran:31:17	Vishnu, Dhata, Bhaga, Pusha, Mitra, Indra, Varuna, Aryaman, Vivasvan, Amshuman, Tvashta, and the twelfth, Parjanya, are remembered.
brahmapuran:31:18	These twelve Adityas are established separately; they rise always in order by the twelve months.
brahmapuran:31:19	Vishnu burns in Chaitra, and Aryaman in Vaishakha; Vivasvan in the month of Jyeshtha, and Amshuman in Ashadha is remembered;
brahmapuran:31:20	Parjanya in the month of Shravana, Varuna in the month called Prausthapada, Indra in the month of Ashvayuja, Dhata burns in Kartika;
brahmapuran:31:21	likewise Mitra in Margashirsha, Pusha the day-maker in Pausha, Bhaga is to be known in Magha, Tvashta burns in Phalguna.
brahmapuran:31:22	Vishnu always shines with twelve hundred rays; Aryaman shines with a thousand and three hundred;
brahmapuran:31:23	Vivasvan with twice seven (hundred); Amshuman with five and three; Parjanya like Vivasvan, and Varuna and Aryaman likewise;
brahmapuran:31:24	the revered Tvashta like Mitra, with a thousand and a hundred; Indra with twice six (hundred); Dhata with eleven hundred;
brahmapuran:31:25	Mitra with a thousand; Pusha with nine hundred. At the northern course of the Sun the rays increase,
brahmapuran:31:26	and at the southern course the Sun's rays decrease again. Thus the thousand rays from the Sun's world are a favour.
brahmapuran:31:27	Thus twenty-four names, of which one has been told of these; the thousand has been told in detail again elsewhere.
brahmapuran:31:28	What merit, Lord of creatures, and what goal, Supreme Lord, do those obtain who praise the Sun with his thousand names?"

Listen, tigers among sages, to the essence, the eternal: enough of the thousand names; reciting this auspicious hymn is sufficient.
brahmapuran:31:30	I shall tell you the names that are secret, pure and auspicious; listen to those of the Sun.
brahmapuran:31:31	Vikartana, Vivasvan, Martanda, Bhaskara, Ravi, Lokaprakashaka, Shriman, Lokachakshu, Maheshvara,
brahmapuran:31:32	Lokasakshi, Trilokesha, Kartri, Hartri, Tamisraha, Tapana, Tapana (the scorcher), Shuchi, Saptashvavahana,
brahmapuran:31:33	Gabhastihasta, Brahma, Sarvadevanamaskrita: this hymn of twenty-one names is ever dear to the Sun.
brahmapuran:31:34	It gives health of body, increase of wealth and fame; it is famed as the King of Hymns, renowned in the three worlds.
brahmapuran:31:35	He who, pure, praises the Sun with this at the two twilights, at sunrise and sunset, is freed from all sins.
brahmapuran:31:36	Whatever is done by mind, speech, body or action is all destroyed by a single recitation in the Sun's presence.
brahmapuran:31:37	A single recitation, the fire-offering, the twilight worship, the incense mantra, the arghya mantra and the offering mantra,
brahmapuran:31:38	in giving of food and in gifts, in prostration and circumambulation, this great mantra, worshipped, is auspicious and removes all sin.
brahmapuran:31:39	Therefore you, Brahmins, with effort, should praise with this hymn the boon-giving god who grants the fruit of all desires.
Tvashta, appeased and bowed to by Vishvakarma the Prajapati, gave his daughter named Samjna to Vivasvan.
The lord of rays begot three children on her: two very fortunate sons and a daughter, Yamuna.
By that excessive brilliance of Martanda Vivasvan he scorched the three worlds with the moving and unmoving.
Seeing that form, round like a globe, Samjna, unable to bear Vivasvan's great brilliance, spoke to her shadow:

I shall go, may you be well, to my father's own house; you must stay here unchanged by my command, auspicious one.
brahmapuran:32:54	These two boys of mine and the lovely daughter must be cared for; and you must not tell this to the lord.
Goddess, until hair is seized or until a curse, I shall never tell your intention; go where you wish.
Thus addressed, Samjna, ashamed, went to her father's house; she stayed in her father's house for a thousand years.
Told repeatedly by her father, "Go to your husband's side," she became a mare and went to the northern Kurus.
There the virtuous one practised austerity, fasting, Brahmins, intent on her promise, when Samjna had gone to her father's side.
The shadow, bearing her form, approached the Sun; and the lord Sun, thinking "this is Samjna,"
likewise begot two sons and a daughter. Samjna of the earth (the shadow) made for those children of her own
an affection not as for the earlier-born; Manu tolerated that of hers, but Yama did not bear it.
Greatly pained and much distressed by his father's wife, Yama, out of anger, childishness and by force of the destined event, threatened her with his foot, but did not strike her body.
Since you threaten with your foot your father's wife, who is greater, therefore this foot of yours will fall, no doubt.
Yama, his mind greatly pained by that curse, the righteous-souled one, along with Manu, reported everything to his father:

Mother, god, does not behave toward us with equal affection; leaving aside the elder, she wishes to favour the younger with love.
brahmapuran:32:66	My foot was raised against her but not dropped on her body; from childishness or delusion, you ought to forgive it.
brahmapuran:32:67	I have been cursed in anger, father, by one who is a mother as my mother; therefore I do not think her a mother, best of the burning.
brahmapuran:32:68	By your grace, revered one, think how this foot of mine may not fall by my mother's curse today, lord of cattle.

Without doubt, son, there will be a great cause here by which anger entered you, a knower of dharma, righteous by nature.
brahmapuran:32:70	For all curses there is a counter; but for those cursed by a mother there is nowhere any turning back of the curse.
brahmapuran:32:71	This word of your mother cannot be made false; out of love for my son I will grant you some favour:
brahmapuran:32:72	worms, taking flesh, will go to the earth; her word will be true, and you will be saved.
Aditya said to the shadow: "Why have you shown greater affection toward one among your sons who are all equal?
Surely you are not their mother, you are some Samjna come here; a mother does not curse even her virtueless children."
She, avoiding that and afraid of the curse, told the Sun the account; having heard it, he went to his father-in-law.
And he, duly honouring the Sun then, soothed him as he wished to burn him in anger, and said:

This your form is suffused with excessive brilliance, very hard to bear, and Samjna, unable to bear it, roams in the forest, practising austerity.
brahmapuran:32:78	You will see her today, your own well-conducted wife, practising great austerity in the forest for the sake of a form for you.
brahmapuran:32:79	I have heard Brahma's word about checking your brilliance. I shall fashion today a form of yours that is pleasing, lord of heaven.
Then the revered Sun said to Tvashta, "So be it." Then Vivasvan's form had been round.
Vishvakarma, permitted by Vivasvan, in Shakadvipa mounted him on a lathe and began to trim away that brilliance.
While the radiant one, who was the centre of all the worlds, was being turned, the earth with oceans, mountains and forests rose up to the sky.
The whole sky, Brahmins, with moon, planets and stars, fortunate ones, was thrown downward and in confusion.
All the oceans too had their waters scattered; the great mountains were split, their peaks and bases shattered.
All the Dhruva-supported stations, best of sages, went down, their bonds of rays-ties snapping.
Thousands of great clouds, flung by the winds from the whirling motion, were broken, uttering terrible roars.
The earth, sky and nether regions, bewildered by the whirling of the Sun, became the world in great confusion, best of sages.
Seeing the three worlds in confusion and revolving, the gods and sages with Brahma praised the Sun:

You are the primal god of the gods, born for the welfare of the earth; in the times of creation, preservation and end you stand in a threefold division.
brahmapuran:32:90	May it be well with you, lord of the world, day-maker, rainer of heat! Then Indra and the other gods praised him, even as he was being carved.
brahmapuran:32:91	Victory, god, lord of the world! Victory, lord of the whole world! Then the seven sages, led by Vasishtha and Atri,
praised him with various hymns, saying "May it be well, may it be well"; with excellent Vedic words the Valakhilyas praised him.
Agni and the others, joyfully, as he was being carved, said: "You, lord, are the liberation of the seekers of liberation; you are the highest object of meditation for the meditators.
You are the goal of all beings, engaged in the course of rites; you are worthy of worship, lord of gods; may there be well-being for us, lord of the worlds.
May there be well-being always for our two-footed and for our four-footed." Then the hosts of Vidyadharas, Yakshas, Rakshasas and serpents,
with joined palms, bowing their heads to the Sun, uttered many kinds of words pleasing to the mind and ears:
May your brilliance be tolerable, creator of beings, to beings. Then Haha, Huhu, Narada and Tumburu,
skilled Gandharvas, began to sing to the Sun, expert in the three modes of song, Shadja, Madhyama and Gandhara,
with modulations, beats and combinations, giving delight; Vishvachi, Ghritachi, Urvashi, Tilottama,
Menaka, Sahajanya and Rambha, the best of the Apsarases, danced as the Sun, lord of the worlds, was being carved.
Performing many dramatic expressions of sentiment, gesture and play, they then had played lutes, flutes and the like, cymbals,
small drums, large drums, mridangas, paṭahas, divine kettledrums and conches, by hundreds and thousands.
With singing and dancing Gandharvas and hosts of Apsarases, and with the sound of instruments, everything was made tumultuous.
Then all the deities, with joined palms, their forms bent with devotion, bowed to the thousand-rayed one as he was being carved.
Then in that uproar, at the gathering of all the gods, Vishvakarma slowly trimmed away the brilliance.
Carved skilfully by Vishvakarma down to the knees, he did not approve of the carving, and was therefore taken down.
But the form was not harmed by the removal of brilliance; a form lovelier than lovely then shone more.
Thus, at the time of cold, water and heat, he who is praised by Shiva, Brahma and Vishnu — hearing of the carving of the Sun, one goes to the Sun's world at the end of life.
Thus, best of sages, was the Sun's birth in the past, and his supreme form has been recounted by me.
Unknowable, imperceptible, beyond meditation, imperishable, without beginning or end: salutation to that form of yours.

Salutations again and again to the cause of causes; salutations again and again to the liberator from sin; salutation to you, destroyer of the Daityas; salutations again and again to the liberator from disease.
Salutations again and again to the giver of all boons; to the giver of all happiness; to the giver of all wealth; to the giver of all understanding.
Thus praised, the revered one, assuming a brilliant form, spoke in a gracious voice: "What boon shall be given to you?"
Your form is exceedingly brilliant, no one can bear it; may it be bearable, Lord, for the good of the world.
Saying "So be it," the lord, the primal maker, for the accomplishment of the worlds' work, giver of heat, rain and cold,
then Sankhyas, Yogis, and others seeking liberation, meditating, meditate on the Day-maker god residing in the heart.
Even one devoid of all marks or joined with all sins crosses over all sin by taking refuge in the god Arka.
Agnihotra, Vedas, sacrifices with many fees do not equal a sixteenth part of the bow of devotion to the Sun.
The supreme of tirthas, the auspicious of auspicious things, the pure of pure things: they take refuge in the Day-maker.
